ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZjzaIg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDKf5s", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 69, "title": "Implement scheduled WD2793 Read Address for both disk interfaces", "body": "## Problem

`crates/msx-core/src/disk.rs:444` immediately rejects Read Address with record-not-found. `tests/disk.rs:318` explicitly expects that rejection. Disk software therefore cannot inspect sector IDs, even on supported normal raw images.

Read Address should return the next encountered ID through six clocked Data-register transfers. This is a missing hardware capability shared by MSX1/MSX2 and both disk interfaces; no commercial-game failure has been observed.

## Expected outcome

Implement scheduled Read Address, including documented C0h/C4h commands, within the existing 360/720 KiB normal-MFM profile. Reuse rotational search and fractional deadlines while preserving existing sector commands and media ownership.

Keep Read Track, Write Track/formatting, additional image formats, full HLD modeling and unrelated controller timing corrections outside this task.

## Context

Baseline: `61b2ee1b0291f7e6e64a1785c15df8f33c5c0ff5`; clean local HEAD matches inspected GitHub main. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. Previous disk Issues #57, #59 and #61 cover sector searches, byte transfers and FORCE INTERRUPT; Read Address remains absent.

Relevant paths include `crates/msx-core/src/disk.rs`, bus/scheduling in `src/lib.rs`, native disk/Philips tests, `tests/fixtures/philips.py`, `tests/philips.spec.js`, and `docs/disks.md`.

Authoritative behavior and applicable references:

- [TI second-source TMS279X/WD279X documentation](https://deramp.com/swtpc.com/DC_5/TMS279X_DataSheet.pdf), printed pp. 10, 13, 23 and 39–40: command flags, settling, six ID bytes, CRC checking, cylinder-to-Sector update and command/status behavior. This is an edited manufacturer transcription, without physical WD2793 confirmation.
- [Pinned openMSX WD2793](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/WD2793.cc): next-ID selection and Type-III sequencing. Its missing-ID timeout is explicitly TODO and its read servicing must not become an unquestioned timing oracle.
- [Synthetic normal-track construction](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/SectorBasedDisk.cc) and [ID decoding](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/RawTrack.cc): CHRN fields and MFM CRC coverage/order. Raw DSK contains payloads, requiring synthesized IDs rather than metadata inferred from payload bytes.

Existing native suites cover Types I/II/IV and Philips integration. [Inspected CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/40069225731/job/120798847427) report 284 Rust and 184 browser passes, including the current rejection assertion. These results do not validate Read Address. No builds or tests ran during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Accept Read Address through both existing interfaces. Sample READY, apply E settling using the existing 1 MHz/HLT-high profile, then search rotation for the next available ID. Do not filter by Track/Sector registers or inherit Type-II side-compare, multi-record or write state. Return the physical cylinder and selected recorded side; a deliberately mismatched Track register must not prevent success.
- [ ] Transfer exactly `C,H,R,N,CRC-high,CRC-low`, with N=02h and R=1..9. Set Sector to the returned cylinder, preserving Track and physical head position. Compute normal MFM CRC over `A1 A1 A1 FE C H R N`, polynomial 1021h, initial FFFFh. Independent expected examples are `00 00 01 02 CA 6F` and `02 01 03 02 76 55`. Write protection must not reject this read.
- [ ] Drive arrivals from absolute device deadlines at the existing rational 32 µs byte cadence. Data reads acknowledge only the current request; signal/status polling cannot advance bytes. Missed arrivals replace unread data, retain LOST DATA and continue to timed completion. Explicitly document and test first-byte, final-byte service and completion boundaries, distinguishing selected timing conventions from physically confirmed edges. Preserve the existing final-byte service convention unless stronger evidence supports a correction.
- [ ] Use Type-III status and ordinary completion IRQ/acknowledgement while preserving the immediate IRQ latch. Synthesized valid IDs have clear CRC error; unsupported-side searches produce no fabricated ID. Document and test the selected no-ID fifth-index timeout as a profile convention, retaining matching-ID-before-index ordering. Raw DSK cannot supply damaged-ID CRCs; do not introduce a new media format merely to test that unavailable input.
- [ ] Cover FORCE INTERRUPT, reset, mount/eject, interface removal and effective drive/side/motor changes during settling, search and transfer. Extend the existing transfer-cancellation policy consistently; canceled work cannot resume. Equivalent Philips selectors/unused latch bits must retain their current behavior. Preserve dirty guards, completed writes and exact image exports.
- [ ] Add independent native timestamp/status/byte expectations covering both geometries and recorded sides, multiple cylinders, successive IDs and rotational wrap, E=0/1, boundary starts, no READY/no ID, starvation and recovery. Assert large, irregular and single-cycle tick equivalence. Replace the obsolete rejection expectation and demonstrate baseline-sensitive failures without deriving all expectations from production helpers.
- [ ] Extend original Z80 fixtures and native/compiled-Wasm tests to obtain and check ID bytes through real mapped registers on both models/interfaces/geometries, with browser coverage at `/` and `/msx-rust/`. Include serviced and unserviced transfers, Reset and exact exported-image checks. No host BIOS shortcuts, proprietary firmware or gameplay prerequisites.
- [ ] Preserve MSX1/MSX2 slots/mapper, firmware coexistence, PSG/SCC/SCC-I/FM audio, SRAM persistence, cassette, browser lifecycle and local-data/provenance safeguards. Update affected hardware documentation and original-fixture licensing; avoid unrelated UI or controller-framework changes.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs and accurately reports README checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, with documented dependency setup, fixture reproducibility and whitespace checks. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review under `docs/review-guidelines.md`; resolve blocking findings and distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed validation.

## Optional validation

Before merge, compare the original ID/CRC trace with a pinned upstream configuration. Record configuration differences and upstream timing limitations. This comparison has not been performed and is not required for acceptance. Diagnostic success alone does not establish commercial playability.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
